title: Show HN: Subvocal – Talk to your computer without making noise
why_read: A novel silent-speech-to-text interface project that is genuinely interesting from a signal-processing and HCI engineering perspective.
analysis: Subvocal appears to be a device or software project that lets users communicate with a computer by detecting subvocalization or subtle muscle movements rather than audible speech. This is a hard and interesting engineering problem involving EMG or similar sensing, signal processing, and real-time classification. If it is a working open-source show-and-tell, it is a good example of applied biosignal engineering outside typical software work. The strong engagement suggests genuine novelty rather than hype.
